text:
UTA arrives with the better process and the worse results. The Mammoth are 2-2-1 in their last five, outscored 20-16, and lost 4-2 at OTT four days ago while playing without John Marino and Kailer Yamamoto (both on injured reserve), and Nate Schmidt. Andrew Peeke has moved in beside Schmidt and is up to 20:20 a night from 14:46. VGK has won three straight, most recently 4-1 at BUF, though without Noah Hanifin and Parker Wotherspoon. This is also a rematch of last spring's first-round series, which the Golden Knights won in six. That history isn't in our numbers.

At five on five, UTA has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 52% for VGK, and our model gives VGK only a slight edge tonight, 3.23 to 3.01. The UTA penalty kill allows 0.68 expected goals a game to VGK's 0.49, and UTA takes 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Karel Vejmelka is 7.2 goals saved above expected below par this season, though he was 5.4 above last year. Projected VGK starter Carter Hart is 2.1 above this season after being 4.4 below last year.

Our model gives Logan Cooley (33% to score) a good look; he is hot, with 13 points in 10 games, though due to cool. Clayton Keller has a five-game point streak, and ESPN noted his goal against OTT. For VGK, Mark Stone is at 35% to score, and Jack Eichel is the likeliest to record two or more points (37%). As The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn posted, Eichel scored to make it 2-0 against BUF, then raised his arms to the crowd.
